findings.title: wikipedia_embeddings.ipynb cells 17/19: published outputs show a stale unrelated figure plus duplicate plots (reproduced on fresh execution)
findings.description: Cells 17 and 19 are the only plot cells that do not assign hyp.plot()'s return value, so each renders TWICE (execute_result of the returned Figure + the shown figure). Worse, cell 17 additionally displays the LEFTOVER animation figure from cell 10 (hyp.plot(..., animate='spin', save_path=..., show=False) leaves its figure pyplot-registered; see finding 002): an untitled 3,136-point cluster map appears sandwiched between the two copies of the 20-point live-keywords plot. This is baked into the SHIPPED notebook's stored outputs (cell 17 has 3 image outputs, cell 19 has 2), so the published tutorial page renders a confusing stray figure mid-narrative. Fresh end-to-end execution reproduces it exactly. Fix: assign (fig = hyp.plot(...)) or add trailing ';' in cells 17/19, and close the cell-10 figure after saving (import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; plt.close(fig)) -- or fix the show=False animation leak in code (finding 002).

findings.title: 1-channel streaming input (e.g. single-sensor LSL device: EDA/PPG/respiration) crashes hyp.plot with a bare IndexError; static path handles the same shape fine
findings.description: hyp.plot(hyp.io.lsl_stream(...)) on a 1-channel outlet crashes at the first redraw with 'IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 1' from hypertools/io/streaming.py:264 (artist.set_data(full[:, 0], full[:, 1]) assumes >=2 columns whenever is3d is False). Single-channel LSL sources are common in psychophysiology (EDA, PPG, respiration, temperature), and lsl_stream()'s docstring advertises 'an EEG amplifier, eye tracker, or any other application publishing via a pylsl.StreamOutlet'. The STATIC path is fine with the same shape -- hyp.plot(np.ndarray (60,1)) works (interpolated 900-point line) -- so this is a streaming-only regression of otherwise-supported input. 2-channel and 3-channel streams work ((60,2) and (60,3) verified). Fix sketch: when head_red has 1 column, plot against sample index (pad a column) as the static path effectively does, or raise a clear ValueError naming the limitation.

findings.title: wikipedia tutorial: unseeded UMAP re-fit per plot call makes the density-overlay cell a DIFFERENT map than the preceding cell; with n=20 a category's glow can vanish entirely
findings.description: Cells 17 and 19 each call hyp.plot(live_embeddings, ..., reduce='UMAP') so UMAP is re-fit unseeded; the 'volumetric density overlay' plot has a completely different layout than the plot it narratively extends ('adds a translucent volumetric KDE glow around each colored group'). In our real run the second UMAP fit merged the 5 'neuroscience' points into the 'music' cluster: the red group has NO visible glow and its points are buried under cyan (wiki_cell19_5.png vs the clean shipped_wiki_cell19_out0.png). The shipped stored outputs also show two different layouts between cells 17 and 19. Verified fix: pass reduce={'model': 'UMAP', 'kwargs': {'random_state': 42}} in both cells (seeded runs produce identical layouts; unseeded runs do not).

findings.actual: unseeded identical: False / seeded identical: True. Fresh notebook run: cell 19 plot shows only green/cyan/purple glows; the 5 red 'neuroscience' points are inside the cyan cluster with no red glow (wiki_cell19_5.png), while cell 17's layout (wiki_cell17_2.png) had them separated.

findings.title: lsl_streaming.ipynb cleanup cell prints an alarming liblsl 'ERR| Stream transmission broke off' line (present in shipped outputs too) because the inlet is never closed
findings.description: Cell 9 stops the outlet thread but never closes the stream generator opened in cell 6, so the still-open pylsl inlet detects the broken connection and liblsl logs 'ERR| Stream transmission broke off (Input stream error.); re-connecting...' into the cell's output. The shipped notebook's stored cell-9 output contains this line verbatim, so the published tutorial's 'Cleaning up' section ends on an unexplained error message. Reproduced in both fresh end-to-end runs this audit. Adding stream.close() before stopping the outlet closes the inlet cleanly (verified: generator .close() runs inlet.close_stream() without error), or a one-line narrative note would defuse it.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import threading, time, gc
import pylsl, hypertools as hyp
info = pylsl.StreamInfo('AuditErrRepro', 'EEG', 4, 100.0, 'float32', 'audit-err')
outlet = pylsl.StreamOutlet(info); stop = threading.Event()
def push():
    i = 0
    while not stop.is_set(): outlet.push_sample([float(i)] * 4); i += 1; time.sleep(0.01)
th = threading.Thread(target=push, daemon=True); th.start()
stream = hyp.io.lsl_stream(name='AuditErrRepro', timeout=5.0)
next(stream)
stop.set(); th.join(); del outlet; gc.collect()
time.sleep(3)  # liblsl prints ERR| Stream transmission broke off ... to stderr"

findings.title: gif-conversion cells fail cryptically on machines without ffmpeg (silent skip, then FileNotFoundError at Image display; mp4 orphaned)
findings.description: HF cell 13 and wiki cell 11 guard the ffmpeg conversion with 'if shutil.which("ffmpeg"):' but the trailing Image('<name>.gif') sits OUTSIDE the guard. Without ffmpeg (common on local machines; markdown mentions ffmpeg only in passing), the cell silently skips conversion, then the Image display fails at render time with FileNotFoundError -- IPython's formatter logs a traceback and degrades the output to text/plain, and the exported .mp4 is left behind un-displayed (HF deletes it only inside the ffmpeg branch). An else-branch (e.g. print('ffmpeg not found -- animation left as hf_embeddings_spin.mp4')) plus moving Image() into the guarded branch would fail gracefully.

findings.title: stream_max is silently exceeded when smaller than stream_init: the head is fully consumed first (default stream_init=10000 -> hyp.plot(stream, stream_max=500) consumes 10000 samples)
findings.description: plot()'s docstring for stream_max says 'stop streaming after this many samples', but plot_stream() consumes the full stream_init head BEFORE the stream_max check runs: with stream_init=50 and stream_max=20, 50 samples are consumed and plotted (stream_info['n_samples']=50). With the DEFAULTS (stream_init=10000), a user who writes hyp.plot(stream, stream_max=500) to cap consumption of a rate-limited/expensive stream actually pulls 10,000 samples. No warning is emitted. Fix sketch: clamp the head to min(stream_init, stream_max) (models then fit on stream_max samples) or document the interaction and warn when stream_max < stream_init.
findings.expected: at most stream_max=20 samples consumed, or a warning/error that stream_max < stream_init cannot be honored
findings.actual: stream_max=20 < stream_init=50 -> n_samples = 50 | truncated = True  (verified through a real 4-channel LSL outlet as well)

findings.title: backend='plotly' is silently ignored for streaming inputs: returns a matplotlib Figure despite the backend docstring promising 'With the plotly backend, the return value is a plotly Figure'
findings.description: hyp.plot(stream, ..., backend='plotly') runs the matplotlib streaming path and returns matplotlib.figure.Figure with no warning or error. The backend parameter's docstring states unconditionally that with the plotly backend the return value is a plotly Figure; the streaming docs never carve out an exception. A user on Colab (where backend='auto' resolves to plotly) reading the LSL tutorial cannot tell which contract wins. Should either raise ('streaming is matplotlib-only') or warn and document the fallback.
findings.expected: plotly Figure, or a clear error/warning that streaming supports only the matplotlib backend
findings.actual: plotly+stream returned: <class 'matplotlib.figure.Figure'>  (silently; verified through a real 4-channel LSL outlet)

findings.title: wikipedia tutorial claim '2,000 characters (roughly 512 tokens)' does not reproduce: measured ~372 tokens (max 447 over 100 articles)
findings.description: Cell 5 markdown: 'we truncate each article to its first 2,000 characters (roughly 512 tokens)'. Tokenizing the first 2,000 characters of 100 corpus articles with the tutorial's own model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) gives mean 372 / median 374 / max 447 tokens -- no article comes near 512. The engineering rationale (stay within the model's 512-token window) is sound; the parenthetical number is wrong by ~27%. Suggest '(comfortably within the model's 512-token limit)' or '(roughly 370-450 tokens)'.
findings.repro:
/Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import hypertools as hyp
m = SentenceTransformer('BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5')
wiki = hyp.load('wiki')
counts = [len(m.tokenizer(str(d)[:2000])['input_ids']) for d in wiki[0].ravel()[:100]]
print('mean=%.0f median=%.0f min=%d max=%d' % (np.mean(counts), np.median(counts), min(counts), max(counts)))"
findings.expected: ~512 tokens per truncated article, per the markdown
findings.actual: token counts for first-2000-chars over 100 articles: mean=372 median=374 min=137 max=447

findings.title: legend-length mismatch error message names 'label=' although the user passed legend=, and calls hue groups 'dataset(s)'
findings.description: hyp.plot(X, 'o', hue=<3 groups>, legend=['only-one']) raises: "label= was given as a list/tuple of length 1, but there are 3 dataset(s) to plot...". The user never passed label= (they passed legend=, per the tutorials' own usage in hugging_face_embeddings cell 6), and their single dataset was split into 3 hue groups internally -- both terms in the message refer to internals, not to what the user typed. The length rule itself is correct and enforced; only the wording misleads.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
X = np.vstack([rng.normal(loc=(0,0,0), size=(30,3)), rng.normal(loc=(8,0,0), size=(30,3)), rng.normal(loc=(0,8,0), size=(30,3))])
labels = ['alpha']*30 + ['beta']*30 + ['gamma']*30
hyp.plot(X, 'o', hue=labels, legend=['only-one'], reduce=None, show=False)"
findings.expected: error message that references legend= and hue groups, e.g. 'legend= has 1 entry but hue defines 3 groups'
findings.actual: ValueError :: label= was given as a list/tuple of length 1, but there are 3 dataset(s) to plot; pass either a single value (broadcast to every dataset) or a list/tuple of length 3.

findings.description: hyp.plot(X, 'o', reduce='UMPA') (plausible typo of the tutorials' reduce='UMAP') raises a ValueError whose text embeds source-indentation whitespace ('fit_transform          methods') and cites http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html -- the 0.8-era API page (currently redirects 301->200, but it is the legacy page layout that the 1.0 docs restructure replaces). Compare the cluster-typo message, which is exemplary ('unknown cluster model ...; supported names: ...').

import hypertools as hyp
hyp.plot(np.random.rand(20, 5), 'o', reduce='UMPA', show=False)"

findings.title: lsl_stream(name=123) raises a cryptic pylsl-internal TypeError that never names the offending parameter
findings.description: Passing a non-string name (e.g. an int, a plausible slip when stream ids are numeric) surfaces pylsl's internal string-encoding failure: "descriptor 'encode' for 'str' objects doesn't apply to a 'int' object" -- no mention of lsl_stream, name=, or the fix. A one-line isinstance check in lsl_stream() (mirroring the excellent no-stream-found HypertoolsIOError) would name the problem. Same passthrough style as the documented **resolve_kwargs forwarding (which is fine for kwargs), but name/type are lsl_stream's OWN parameters.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import hypertools as hyp
hyp.io.lsl_stream(name=123, timeout=0.5)"
findings.expected: TypeError/ValueError naming the parameter, e.g. 'name= must be a string (the LSL name property), got int'
findings.actual: RAISED builtins.TypeError :: descriptor 'encode' for 'str' objects doesn't apply to a 'int' object

findings.title: spin GIFs shipped twice: as tracked .gif files AND base64-embedded in notebook stored outputs (~25 MB combined for two tutorials)
findings.description: hugging_face_embeddings.ipynb is 14.77 MB and wikipedia_embeddings.ipynb is 9.3 MB because each embeds its spin GIF (10.9 MB / 6 MB) base64 in the stored Image() output -- while the identical GIFs are ALSO tracked as standalone files (docs/tutorials/hf_embeddings_spin.gif, wikipedia_embeddings_spin.gif) for use elsewhere. Every clone/docs build carries both copies. Consider Image(url=...) / markdown image reference to the shipped gif, stripping the embedded output, or reducing frame count (900 frames at 420px for HF).
findings.expected: tutorial sources a few hundred KB; large binaries stored once
findings.actual: hugging_face_embeddings.ipynb 14.77 MB; wikipedia_embeddings.ipynb 9.3 MB; plus hf_embeddings_spin.gif 10.94 MB and wikipedia_embeddings_spin.gif 6.56 MB tracked separately (shipped cell 13 output: ('stream', ('gif: 10.9 MB',)), ('execute_result', ['image/gif', ...]))
